findings.class: GENUINE-FAIL (port divergence — FILED, not fixed in-pass; verification-only fence)
findings.mechanism: createdAt serialization precision. Java Jackson JSR-310 renders Instant with the DB timestamp(6) micros via shortest-round-trip fraction (e.g. '2026-10-04T09:37:00.129532Z'); the port renders fixed milliseconds via JS Date ISO ('2026-10-04T09:37:00.129Z'). Deep-diff evidence: teacher-detail has EXACTLY ONE divergence (@ .createdAt); teacher-listing has 1021 divergences, ALL @ .N.createdAt with identical semantics.
findings.port_author_preview: The canonical contract's own header (packages/contracts/src/content.ts:25-28) anticipated exactly this: 'Instant fields ... JS Date.toISOString() caps at milliseconds ... Golden tolerance treats these as volatile fields UNTIL A REAL-DATA CAPTURE SAYS OTHERWISE.' The F-5 real-data capture (merged via #16) now exists and pins full precision — the deferral has matured; the port's ISO writer needs Instant.toString() shortest-round-trip semantics (render the DB fractional digits trimmed of trailing zeros).
findings.fix_sketch: port-side ISO writer change (format the DB timestamp fraction verbatim, trailing-zero-trimmed, instead of Date round-trip); affects content view assembly only; unit pins updated; re-run of Pass B expected 13/15 after fix (F-2 remains)

findings.class: GENUINE-FAIL (port divergence — FILED, not fixed in-pass)
findings.mechanism: Page-text assembly returns EMPTY for a real text page: expected 716 chars of page-4 text ('The list shows some techniques used to separate mixtures...') for doc 853ae02d-0090-4c40-89ef-b69681c8bb40, actual ''. The sibling cases PASS: page=1 cover-empty (honestly empty on the capture side too) and page=99 bounds-404 — so range checks and the corpus-law gate are correct; the TEXT YIELD of the assembly (reader.ts collect() over doc.textBlocks/tables/equations filtered by pageNumber===page, verbatim DocumentPageText.of port) produces nothing for a page the capture proves has text. The doc query feeding the assembly (repositories.ts) is the prime suspect (shape/column mismatch), to be traced by the owner lane; the capture COW and this run's COW share the same production parent, so the DATA side is identical.
findings.impact: learner citation reader serves no page text for real documents — a functional gap, not a formatting one

findings.class: CAPTURE-STABILITY (R6/R0 ruling required — NOT a port defect)
findings.owner: R6 golden-master steward / R0 (same family as T-MIG-013's re-capture stability probe follow-up)
findings.mechanism: versions[] ORDERING: set-compare diagnostic (setcheck.ts) proves SAME multiset — 6/6 versionIds, 6/6 questionIds, paper header identical — in a DIFFERENT sequence. The frozen core's queryVersions path is questionVersions.findByPaperId(paperId), a Spring Data derived query with NO ORDER BY (ContentReviewService.java:869) — unspecified heap order pinned by the capture. The port's findByPaperId (review-repos.ts:125) is equally unordered (faithful). No faithful port can pass this case deterministically; the case over-pins unspecified DB ordering.
findings.options: (a) R6 amends the case to ordering-insensitive comparison for versions[] (tolerate-style rule), or (b) re-capture with a pinned deterministic order — an upstream contract change is FORBIDDEN (C1). Evidence arrays attached in run-001-diagnosis.txt

harness_findings.finding: Bun.serve auto-serve (bun apps/api/src/index.ts) defaults to a 10s request idleTimeout; the 581KB / 1023-row listing over neon-http on cold free-tier compute exceeds it ('[Bun.serve]: request timed out after 10 seconds' + client ECONNRESET). Fixed HARNESS-SIDE via boot-with-timeout.ts (imports the app, serves with idleTimeout=255) — zero api code touched. Recorded for every future live-replay lane.

Harmless for the seed-pinned tranche (they pin emptiness) but the promised behavior does not exist for future curriculum fixed-uuid replays (T-MIG-021's needs). Flagged to r7a/R0; NOT fixed in-pass (tool is a sha-verified verbatim copy per the R0 #20 disposition).
